data-for-the-ledger-boundary.text: As the writer of the next child or of the 1.x tag policy, I build on one fixed vocabulary for transactions, scripts and registry identities.

the-registry-free-library.text: Invoked purposes of a transaction: the spend of every input whose payment credential is a script, the mint of every policy the mint moves, every withdrawal and certificate whose credential is a script.

The staking-free view of a transaction clears the stake credential of every address in inputs, reference inputs and outputs, drops withdrawals and certificates, and drops the redeemers of withdrawal and certificate purposes.

the-registry-instance.text: fold present: some input sits at the address whose payment credential is the state script's hash, carries exactly one unit of the registry identity, and its spend's redeemer is the fold;
terminal: every movement under its own policy in the mint is a burn and there is at least one, or fold present.
The witness decision reads only spent inputs' payment credentials, values and output references, spend redeemers, and the mint under the policy's own identifier.
A terminal attestation is the holder's: the discard touches only the holdings list, and only that one terminal entry.
